body:
This previously crashed due to a missing bounds check when hitting the fast path of a uniquely owned list with an out-of-bounds index.

Issue was introduced in https://github.com/cython/cython/commit/d8071289169b3c07f6ebd7816f5a296d609b0e9c
See https://github.com/cython/cython/pull/7011

comment_data.body:
I think this (and another inconsistency) ends up making the whole thing needlessly confusing.

I think it'd be clearer if `__Pyx_PyList_GetItemRef` was always basically equivalent to `PyList_GetItemRef` so there's never a case where it's not boundschecked. I think the only place where this currently matters is one use in `Optimize.c`
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -1161,15 +1161,17 @@ enum __Pyx_ReferenceSharing {
     #define __Pyx_PyList_GetItemRef(o, i) __Pyx_XNewRef(PyList_GetItem(o, i))
   #endif
 #else
+  // Note: no bounds checking!

comment_data.body: Again, I think this is made more confusing than it needs to be because the same macro means different things in different builds. In that on a GIL CPython build `boundscheck` is ignored. Which is fine for the current uses, but really isn't obvious.
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -1161,15 +1161,17 @@ enum __Pyx_ReferenceSharing {
     #define __Pyx_PyList_GetItemRef(o, i) __Pyx_XNewRef(PyList_GetItem(o, i))
   #endif
 #else
+  // Note: no bounds checking!
   #define __Pyx_PyList_GetItemRef(o, i) __Pyx_NewRef(PyList_GET_ITEM(o, i))
 #endif
 
 
-#if CYTHON_AVOID_THREAD_UNSAFE_BORROWED_REFS && !CYTHON_COMPILING_IN_LIMITED_API && CYTHON_ASSUME_SAFE_MACROS
-  #define __Pyx_PyList_GetItemRefFast(o, i, unsafe_shared) (__Pyx_IS_UNIQUELY_REFERENCED(o, unsafe_shared) ? \
+#if CYTHON_AVOID_THREAD_UNSAFE_BORROWED_REFS && !CYTHON_COMPILING_IN_LIMITED_API && CYTHON_ASSUME_SAFE_MACROS && CYTHON_ASSUME_SAFE_SIZE
+  #define __Pyx_PyList_GetItemRefFast(o, i, boundscheck, unsafe_shared) ( \
+    (__Pyx_IS_UNIQUELY_REFERENCED(o, unsafe_shared) && ((!boundscheck) || likely(__Pyx_is_valid_index(i, PyList_GET_SIZE(o))))) ? \
     __Pyx_NewRef(PyList_GET_ITEM(o, i)) : __Pyx_PyList_GetItemRef(o, i))
 #else
-  #define __Pyx_PyList_GetItemRefFast(o, i, unsafe_shared) __Pyx_PyList_GetItemRef(o, i)
+  #define __Pyx_PyList_GetItemRefFast(o, i, boundscheck, unsafe_shared) __Pyx_PyList_GetItemRef(o, i)

comment_data.body: Hmm. I think this one might be ok if we fix the inconsistency in `__Pyx_PyList_GetItemRef`. Disabling `boundscheck` doesn't _force_ it to not happen, it's more of a hint that it's not needed and _can_ be left out if possible and deemed helpful. Which is what happens in the `#if` case here. Now that `boundscheck` is passed into the `…Fast()` macro, it's explicit that the macro takes care of it and calling code doesn't have to.

comment_data.body: This won't work with Limited API plus manually set `CYTHON_AVOID_BORROWED_REFS`. Probably doesn't matter too much because it's a manual combination that I doubt anyone's using
I conditionally replaced the call with `PySequence_GetItem()`.

commit.message:
Check the list index bounds also for uniquely referenced lists.
This previously crashed due to a missing bounds check when hitting the fast path of a uniquely owned list with an out-of-bounds index.
Rename "__Pyx_PyList_GetItemRefFast()" to "__Pyx_PyList_GET_ITEM_REF()" to mark it as not checking index bounds (if possible).
Fix incorrect PyDict_Type usage for PyFrozenDict.
Fix wraparound for "GetItemInt_Fast()" with "avoid borrowed refs".
Call PySequence_ITEM() only if we have it.
Make __Pyx_PyList_GetItemRef() always and consistently apply bounds checking.

title: [Bug] Check the list index bounds also for uniquely referenced lists.
